scene-kit.rationale: Steps carry narration and stable identity, and the host renders the active step’s scene and payload.
evidence: StepMeta declares id, era, title, and caption. Presentation selects steps[nav.index]; Stage renders its Scene with payload, step, and index and uses step.id for ungrouped identity.

scene-kit.rationale: Displayed numbering follows array position rather than authored IDs.
evidence: Header renders index + 1. BrowseFooter derives progress labels and numbers from itemIndex + 1 and the current count from index + 1.

scene-kit.rationale: The generic payload type reaches the presentation boundary and active scene without caller casts.
evidence: Presentation<T> accepts Step<T>[] and passes the selected step to Stage<T>, which forwards its payload to SceneComponent.
Talk passes REFERENCE_STEPS, declared as Step<ReferencePayload>[], directly to Presentation without a cast.
contracts.test.ts includes a valid concrete payload and an expected compile-time error for a missing required payload.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable entity IDs drive an implemented layout-animation mechanism.
evidence: createSceneNode renders motion.div with layout and layoutId={entityId}; Stage encloses scenes in LayoutGroup.
EvolvingScene gives continuing Box entities stable keys and entityId values, preserving their identity across payload updates.

scene-kit.rationale: Newcomer delay does not wait for continuing layout motion to settle.
evidence: constants.ts sets ENTER_DELAY to LAYOUT_T (0.65), but createSceneNode applies duration: ENTER_T (0.35) and delay: ENTER_DELAY to its entire transition, including layout motion. Continuing motion ther…
Appear also uses the fixed ENTER_DELAY and has no completion signal from continuing motion.

scene-kit.rationale: Exit retention covers direct SceneLayer children, but ordinary nested conditional entities can disappear synchronously.
evidence: SceneLayer wraps only its immediate identified children in AnimatePresence; Stage retains whole scene hosts rather than removed descendants within a grouped scene.
EvolvingScene nests conditional ref-ghost and a shrinking card map inside the persistent plain ref-tray div. Moving backward removes those Box children without a surrounding presence boundary.

scene-kit.rationale: Shared group keys preserve the scene host while new payloads update the existing component.
evidence: Stage keys the motion host by groupKey for grouped steps and renders the same Scene component with updated props.
The test 'accepts typed grouped steps, updates the existing scene, and exposes active semantics' navigates between two steps sharing Tracked and a group key, verifies the new payload text, an…

scene-kit.rationale: Continuing grouped children retain their mounted identity, so their initial opacity state is not replayed.
evidence: Stage retains the group-keyed host; SceneLayer preserves explicit child keys; createSceneNode uses initial opacity only on mounting and stable layoutId for subsequent updates.
The reference continuity test rerenders EvolvingScene from through: 3 to through: 4 and asserts ref-card-1 is the identical DOM node while another card appears.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped rendering path preserves authored nesting, coordinates, and overlapping layers.
evidence: SceneLayer clones children only to supply missing keys and forwards authored style; it does not redistribute their positions. Stage scales the complete fixed canvas.
EvolvingScene retains its existing children when adding ref-reveal-frame; presentation CSS positions that frame with absolute inset around the existing diagram.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode renders the active marker and title while omitting reading and previous/next chrome.
evidence: Header’s present branch renders era and position. Footer’s present branch renders the active title instead of BrowseFooter, excluding caption and previous/next controls. Presentation renders Toc only…
The mode-switch test verifies that the caption and table of contents disappear in present mode.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode supplies the required active-step reading chrome.
evidence: BrowseFooter renders the active title, a wrapping paragraph caption, previous/next buttons, numbered progress buttons, and step count. Presentation includes Toc in browse mode.
Host CSS displays the table of contents on wide viewports and hides it below 800px; narration paragraphs are width-constrained without single-line clipping.

scene-kit.rationale: Mode changes leave step position untouched.
evidence: usePresentationNav stores rawIndex and mode independently. toggleMode updates only mode; Presentation continues selecting steps using the unchanged nav.index.

scene-kit.rationale: The required keyboard mappings advance or reverse one step.
evidence: usePresentationNav.onKey maps ArrowRight, Space, and PageDown to next(), and ArrowLeft and PageUp to prev(); both use stepBy with a one-step delta.

scene-kit.rationale: Swipe handling cannot reject predominantly vertical or multi-touch gestures.
evidence: onTouchStart records only touches[0].clientX. onTouchEnd navigates whenever horizontal displacement exceeds 45, without recording vertical coordinates or checking touch count. The focused navigation …

scene-kit.rationale: Progress controls jump to individual steps, and table-of-contents controls jump to section starts.
evidence: BrowseFooter calls onSelect(itemIndex) for progress buttons. Toc computes the first index matching an era and calls onSelect(first). Presentation connects both to nav.goTo.

scene-kit.rationale: Both navigation surfaces expose semantic current state and stable active hooks.
evidence: BrowseFooter compares index with itemIndex; Toc compares the active era. Both emit aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active='true' for the active item.
The grouped-step test verifies aria-current before and after selecting the second progress button.

scene-kit.rationale: The supplied native controls retain their supported keyboard semantics.
evidence: onKey returns for input, textarea, select, and contenteditable targets, and leaves Space/Enter untouched on buttons, links, and role=button targets.

The focused mode-button test dispatches cancelable Space and Enter events and asserts defaultPrevented is false; the editable-control test dispatches ArrowRight from an input and verifies the step st…

scene-kit.rationale: Backward navigation at the first step stays at index zero.
evidence: stepBy routes updates through clampStepIndex, whose lower bound is zero.
The keyboard navigation test sends ArrowLeft at the initial step and asserts activeIndex() is '0'.

scene-kit.rationale: Forward navigation at the last step stays at the final index.
evidence: clampStepIndex bounds indices by stepCount - 1, and stepBy applies that clamp.
The keyboard navigation test reaches index 1 in a two-step deck, sends PageDown, and asserts the index remains '1'.

scene-kit.rationale: The canvas uses one scale factor computed from its actual available stage area.
evidence: useFitScale observes the stage element and feeds its clientWidth/clientHeight to getFitScale, which takes the smaller width and height ratio.
Stage reserves mode-specific top/bottom chrome space and applies transform scale(scale) to the entire authored canvas, using the same factor on both axes.

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered authored canvas defaults to 880×380.
evidence: constants.ts defines DESIGN_W=880 and DESIGN_H=380. Stage consumes those constants as the canvas width and height, and useFitScale uses them as its default design dimensions.

scene-kit.rationale: Primitives and chrome expose stable selectors for author-owned styling.
evidence: createSceneNode emits its supplied class and data hook, merges className, and forwards props. Box, Arrow, Label, Frame, Emphasis, and SymbolChip supply distinct hooks; Appear and SceneLayer emit thei…
Presentation, Stage, Header, Footer, and Toc render stable presentation classes and data attributes.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit rendering supplies motion and geometry without fallback visual treatments.
evidence: The node factory and primitive wrappers add motion, hooks, and accessibility attributes without colors, fonts, borders, shadows, or card styling. SceneLayer and Stage inline styles provide geometry o…
Presentation and chrome render semantic markup and hooks without theme imports or visual style declarations.

scene-kit.rationale: The reusable kit’s implementation does not require a styling framework.
evidence: package.json declares React and Motion runtime dependencies without a styling-framework dependency.
The rendering path uses ordinary DOM classes, inline geometry, React, and Motion; the primitive modules delegate to the same framework-neutral node factory.

scene-kit.rationale: Authors can supply literal coordinates and arbitrary scene children without kit layout restrictions.
evidence: createSceneNode forwards style and other motion props to motion.div. SceneLayer preserves children and merges authored style into its canvas layer.
EvolvingScene supplies literal left/top/width coordinates to primitives; Stage renders the authored Scene directly inside LayoutGroup, allowing custom motion elements as well.

scene-kit.rationale: The default link exists, but the kit itself does not position it bottom-right.
evidence: Footer renders 'made by and-scene' with DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTION_URL but supplies no positioning.
The bottom-right rule comes from host-owned src/index.css: .presentation-attribution uses position:absolute, right:1rem, and bottom:1rem. The bootstrap copy likewise places this rule outside the kit.

scene-kit.rationale: The attribution exposes stable CSS targets.
evidence: Footer’s default anchor emits className='presentation-attribution' and data-presentation-attribution, allowing presentation or host styles to target it.

scene-kit.rationale: Header branding is empty by default and explicitly host-supplied.
evidence: Presentation accepts an optional brand and forwards it to Header without a default value. Header renders only that value in presentation-brand and inserts no default and-scene brand link.

evidence: SKILL.md §1 says to gather details 'one question at a time' and conditionally asks for missing topic, visual style, and step details.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy expressly permits implementation with incomplete detail when the user chooses to proceed.
evidence: SKILL.md §1 requires offering to proceed or continue refining, then says: 'Proceed when the user opts in to partial detail; do not enforce a completeness gate.'

presentation-skill.rationale: Complete prompts can bypass the interview, and individual questions are conditional on missing information.
evidence: SKILL.md §1 states: 'A complete prompt may go straight to implementation.' Topic and style questions apply only when those details are unclear.

presentation-skill.rationale: Template sources resolve relative to the helper's module location, and the executable test exercises copying from a different working directory.

evidence: SKILL.md §2 identifies an empty directory as a standalone root target.

evidence: SKILL.md §2 requires stating the target and missing contracts and waiting for confirmation before writing to a nonempty incomplete project.
INT-001 starts empty and supplies no simulated confirmation, refusal, or pre-confirmation preservation assertions. The helper copies immediately when given valid arguments.

presentation-skill.rationale: The creation policy requires registration, and both delivered and bootstrap routers resolve registered slugs to loaded presentation components.
evidence: SKILL.md §3 requires a unique URL-safe slug and one explicit registry entry.
Both Router functions trim surrounding pathname slashes, look up the slug in a Map built from presentations, and render lazy(route.load) through Suspense.
INT-001 adds a starter registry entry before browser verification; the bootstrap verifier follows registered landing links and checks each route's step state and captions.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy assigns visual design to the presentation or host, and presentation entry components import their own CSS.
evidence: SKILL.md §§2–3 prohibit kit-owned theme defaults and direct visual design into presentation- or host-owned CSS.

presentation-skill.rationale: Explicit preservation instructions govern creation and modification, and the registry supports additive entries.
evidence: SKILL.md §3 requires preserving all existing registry entries and directories when adding a presentation, and preserving unrelated presentation files and routes when modifying one.

presentation-skill.rationale: The modification policy explicitly blocks editing until an unclear target is resolved.
evidence: SKILL.md §1 requires inspecting and listing registered presentations and asking which one to modify before editing when the target is unclear.
The delivered and bootstrap presentations registries expose concrete slug/title entries that support this selection.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy confines modification to the selected presentation and shared files necessary for the requested change.
evidence: SKILL.md §3 says to edit only the selected presentation and necessary registry or shared host files, while preserving unrelated presentation files and routes.
The starter Talk imports local steps and local style.css, supporting presentation-local content and styling changes.

presentation-skill.rationale: The normative completion gate requires build, browser rendering, and browser composition inspection before success.

scene-kit.rationale: The implementation preserves authored nesting, coordinates, and overlapping composition.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode renders the active marker and title while omitting reading navigation chrome.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode provides all required active-step reading elements.
evidence: Footer.tsx renders the active title, paragraph caption, previous/next controls, numbered progress buttons, and step count; Presentation.tsx includes Toc.

scene-kit.rationale: Mode changes do not alter navigation position.

scene-kit.rationale: The required keyboard mappings advance or reverse by one step.
evidence: usePresentationNav.ts maps ArrowRight, Space, and PageDown to stepBy(1), and ArrowLeft and PageUp to stepBy(-1).

scene-kit.rationale: Swipe handling lacks both vertical-displacement and multi-touch rejection.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress and table-of-contents controls directly select their target positions.

scene-kit.rationale: Both navigation surfaces expose semantic and targetable active state.

scene-kit.rationale: The supplied native controls retain their supported editing and activation keys.

scene-kit.rationale: Backward navigation is bounded at zero.

scene-kit.rationale: Forward navigation is bounded at the final step.

Presentation.test.tsx sends PageDown at index 1 in a two-step deck and asserts index remains '1'.

scene-kit.rationale: The canvas uses a single fit factor derived from its actual stage bounds after chrome reservations.

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered authored canvas defaults to 880×380.

scene-kit.rationale: Primitives and presentation chrome expose stable styling selectors.

scene-kit.rationale: The supplied kit adds motion, geometry, and semantic markup without fallback visual styling.
evidence: The node factory and primitive modules contain no default colors, fonts, borders, shadows, or card treatments.
Stage.tsx and SceneLayer.tsx supply geometric inline styles; Presentation.tsx and chrome modules contain no theme imports or visual style declarations.

scene-kit.rationale: The supplied rendering implementation requires no styling framework.
evidence: package.json declares no styling-framework dependency.
The supplied presentation, chrome, and primitive modules use React, Motion, ordinary DOM classes, and inline geometry.

scene-kit.rationale: Authors can retain literal coordinates, custom children, and nested diagrams.

EvolvingScene.tsx supplies literal left/top/width coordinates and custom div/svg children; Stage.tsx renders the authored Scene directly.

scene-kit.rationale: Bottom-right attribution placement comes from host CSS rather than the kit.

scene-kit.rationale: The attribution provides stable host-targetable styling hooks.

presentation-skill.rationale: Complete prompts explicitly bypass the interview.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md §1: 'A complete prompt may go straight to implementation.' Questions about topic, style, and step details apply only when those details are missing.

tests/bootstrap.test.ts invokes the absolute helper path with cwd: tmpdir() for both bootstrap and presentation templates, checks resulting files, and runs npm ci with cwd: materialized.

presentation-skill.rationale: The supplied test lacks the monorepo fixture and root-preservation assertions required for credit.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md §2 specifies a self-contained repository/presentations target and preservation of root build setup.
tests/bootstrap.test.ts constructs no workspace manifest, pnpm workspace, packages directory, or apps directory and does not assert preservation of a monorepo root.
copy-template.mjs accepts an already selected target without repository-layout detection.

presentation-skill.rationale: The explicit standalone-root policy is supported by an executable empty-root scaffold case.

tests/bootstrap.test.ts passes its fresh empty directory directly to the helper, checks package.json and src contracts at that root, and installs and verifies with that directory as cwd.

presentation-skill.rationale: The required confirmation branch evidence is absent from the supplied focused test.

tests/bootstrap.test.ts starts empty and never models an ambiguous nonempty target, user choice, or preservation before confirmation.

presentation-skill.rationale: Explicit preservation instructions are supported by additive registry structures and non-overwriting template copying.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md §3 requires preserving existing registry entries and directories during creation and unrelated presentation files and routes during modification.

evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md §4 begins: 'Do not report success until all checks pass.'
It requires npm run build, browser verification or a Playwright fallback, screenshot inspection, and review of first, last, and densest/key steps.
The completion report prohibits claiming a check passed unless it ran successfully.

presentation-skill.rationale: The completion policy explicitly requires correcting failures and rerunning affected checks.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md §4: 'diagnose and fix failures, then rerun affected checks.'
The same section requires resolving all type/build failures and fixing accidental composition collisions before reporting success.

verification-tooling.rationale: An explicit reachable branch rejects missing canonical registration and produces a nonzero outcome.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs throws when the registry lacks the canonical slug or Talk import; its catch sets process.exitCode = 1.

verification-tooling.rationale: Preview binding, readiness probes, and browser navigation consistently use IPv4 loopback.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs supplies --host 127.0.0.1 and uses http://127.0.0.1:${port} for both fetch readiness and page.goto.

verification-tooling.rationale: A stale responder can satisfy readiness, and subsequent child exit does not fail verification.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs checks preview.exitCode only before fetch and immediately accepts a successful response.

verification-tooling.rationale: The supplied focused tests cover console errors but omit the required page-error propagation case.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs registers console and pageerror listeners and reports failures with activeStep.
tests/reference-verification.test.ts injects console.error at step 7 and asserts its failure message; no scenario injects a page error.

verification-tooling.rationale: The implementation detects blocked navigation, and a focused executable test asserts nonzero failure with the failing step identified.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs waits for the next data-step-index and reports timeout through FAIL: ${activeStep}.
tests/reference-verification.test.ts uses browserFixture({ blocked: true }) and asserts nonzero status, /FAIL: step 1:.*Timeout/, and absence of the success message.

verification-tooling.rationale: A separate project-local inspection command implements browser screenshot capture.
evidence: package.json maps inspect to node scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs.
scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs accepts a slug, starts preview, launches Playwright, and writes page screenshots into artifacts/inspection.

verification-tooling.rationale: The supplied test does not establish that screenshots depict every intended step from the intended preview.
evidence: tests/inspection.test.ts changes only data-step-index and asserts screenshot filenames and a capture message, without verifying captured indices or screenshot content.
scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs clicks Next without asserting the resulting step and accepts HTTP readiness without establishing preview ownership.

verification-tooling.rationale: Capture uses a fixed delay without observing completion or consuming a shared runtime transition contract.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs calls page.waitForTimeout(settleInterval), defaulting to 900 milliseconds.
src/presentation-kit/nodes/createSceneNode.tsx consumes ENTER_T and ENTER_DELAY; the inspection helper consumes neither.
tests/inspection.test.ts asserts elapsed time but contains no animation-completion check.

verification-tooling.rationale: Detection excludes mixed-content text containers, and the supplied regression lacks representative nested text/chrome collision coverage.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs restricts textItems to elements with element.children.length === 0.
tests/inspection.test.ts tests collision between two leaf divs; its nested span is intentionally excluded from detection.

verification-tooling.rationale: A focused executable regression checks intentional-overlap suppression while preserving an unrelated collision warning.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs excludes elements beneath [data-presentation-allow-overlap].
tests/inspection.test.ts positions Intentional overlap beneath that marker, asserts its absence from output, and asserts the Unmarked collision / Collision partner warning remains.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper compares rendered active and inactive styles, and the focused fixture asserts warnings for indistinct progress and missing current TOC state.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs reads computed styles for active and inactive controls, comparing color, background, border, and font weight.
tests/inspection.test.ts gives progress buttons identical styles and TOC buttons no current state, then asserts both corresponding warning messages.

verification-tooling.rationale: A focused executable regression triggers and asserts the browser-default attribution warning.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs flags attribution whose computed textDecorationLine is underline.
tests/inspection.test.ts includes an ordinary attribution anchor and asserts the attribution warning; its .presentation-attribution CSS rule does not match that anchor.
